export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b4b-completion',
  description: 'B4 site-side completion: decisions D17 to D21 (the sparse-picture gate, product identity, Montana-only counts, the live line, plain words), the Montana-first live fetch, the cross-file patch check and the stale docs; one fixer, then a re-check',
  phases: [{ title: 'Fix', detail: 'site, swath words, docs' }, { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, builds, smoke, docs' }],
}
const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b4'
const BASE = 'c860e23'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b4-brief.md'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b4/out'
const KEEP = '/home/user/hail-b4/out/keep'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/hail-store.tar.gz'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4; the module and the site side are in WIP commits, the latest 112c2f3; the part B base for identity checks is ${BASE}). Read ${BRIEF} in full first; its last section "Supervisor decisions after the site build (D17 to D21) and the completion list for part B" is your task list, and the re-check ${OUT}/b4b-recheck.json (its failed_checks and open_items) is the evidence behind it. Product north star: one map; every number next to its unit and kind word; nothing a roofer has to decode. Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first, evidence honesty (a radar estimate is not observed hail and not damage; uncoloured is never "no hail"; stale and unavailable lines end "This is not an all-clear."), plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names, tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package. Never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push; never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (disk is tight: keep scratch small, build at most two sites at a time and delete each when its check is done). The B2 store tar is ${STORE_TAR}. A python with numpy, pygrib and Pillow is ${VENV}; Chromium for Playwright is at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium (PW_CHROMIUM). Network is available. Return a plain report: items applied (file and line), items already in place, items skipped with the reason, commands run with their tails.`
phase('Fix')
const fixR = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\nYou are the completion fixer and you own every file of the branch for this pass. Items: (1) D17: tools/smoke_map.py's hail gate reads as D17 states (zoom to a listed cell at zoom 10 or closer; at least 16 changed pixels at that spot; the note when no cell reaches the floor; the count recorded) with its docstring and test updated; (2) D18: nothing in code; the verification record's B4-2 row reads so; (3) D19: the whole-area count line is dropped from describe() and every count and largest-value word is Montana-only (tests); (4) D20: D37 and DESIGN quote the live line as the module writes it; (5) D21: "this map's area" replaces "the picture" in the D15 sentence and wherever a viewer reads it; "in the window" is replaced by the window's own words in website/templates/about.html (two places) and website/sources.py's hail_swath row; map.js's state tick runs once a minute (STATE_TICK) and the docs say once a minute; PNG sizes read "about 3 KB on a quiet day" in DESIGN and D37; the docs' claim that the sample build fails the 2 percent rule is removed; the "7.8 rebuilds a day" sentence in D37 cites the schedule record in docs/DECISIONS.md D33 or is removed; (6) map.js reads the Montana decision before fetching a live file, so a point outside Montana makes one request, not two (a test in tests/test_site.py's literal and structure scan if it can see it, else the smoke's outside check asserts the request count); (7) apply ${KEEP}/apply_cross_current.py (read it first; it applies the swath fixer's cross-file pairs by exact match and skips pairs already applied) and report which pairs it applied; (8) bring the stale docs named in the re-check to the current code: DESIGN.md section 11 lines 618 to 663 (List and sheet wording, the cadence, the identity sentence, the 2 percent claims), D37, ROADMAP lines 34, 48 and 122, research/globe/validation-evidence/p3-verification.json (B4-7 reads D17; B4-2 reads D18 with the five run times 02:53:58, 03:55:09, 05:45:09, 06:56:57 and 14:23:56 UTC); every number traced to ${OUT}/b4b-recheck.json or the two module re-checks; (9) run ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_site tests.test_swath tests.test_gridded tests.test_storm (tail), build --storm-layers --hail-history --sample --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} into ${OUT}/completionb/sample and run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_map.py on it (tail), then delete the build. Report every item.`, { label: 'fixc:site-completion', phase: 'Fix', model: WORKER })
phase('Recheck')
const recheck = await agent(`Read-only checker in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b4). Read ${BRIEF} (D1 to D21 and the part B completion list) and ${OUT}/b4b-recheck.json. Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/recheckb/ which you create; disk is tight: build one site at a time and delete it when checked. Run and quote: ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests (tail; all must pass); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload; the default build (--sample --now 2026-10-19T02:00:00Z) from a copy of the worktree against the ${BASE} build (diff -rq; only map.js, map.css and their ?v= lines may differ); a live build --storm-layers --hail-history --hail-store ${STORE_TAR} --require-live (allow 10 minutes; say which source failed if one did) and on it PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_map.py --shots (quote the result; the D17 gate's changed-pixel count) and smoke_pages; your own probes in Chromium: the legend words, the view-time state line, the live line on a listed cell (or the no-estimate line) with the D20 wording, one request for a point outside Montana, the SAMPLE credit on the sample build, the Montana-only counts in the List and no-JavaScript words, "this map's area" and no "in the window" anywhere a viewer reads; grep the docs for the stale claims (2 percent, every 10 seconds, 7.8 rebuilds, the old live line); the YAML parses; git -C ${WT} status --short and diff --stat ${BASE}; em-dash and banned-name counts over added lines; the map.js literal scan; the decision 7 audit. Write ${OUT}/b4b-recheck-completion.json with gates B4-1 to B4-7 (status, evidence; B4-2 per D18; B4-7 per D17 with the live preview still pending the push), every completion item done or not done, and the open items. Return that JSON as text and name every check that failed.`, { label: 'recheckb', phase: 'Recheck', model: WORKER })
return { fixR: (fixR || '').slice(0, 6000), recheck }
